explanation: The king of Israel and son of King David, known for his wisdom and the building of the temple in Jerusalem.
The holy place in Jerusalem where the Israelites worshiped God and offered sacrifices; built by King Solomon.
Places where people live and interact, mentioned in 2 Chronicles as places over which Solomon ruled or had influence.
The king of Tyre who helped Solomon obtain materials and labor for the building of the temple.
Fortified buildings or areas used for defense and protection against enemies.
A group of workers or soldiers recruited from the population to carry out specific tasks, such as building the temple.
Gifts, usually food or animals, given to God as a form of worship and gratitude.
Religious leaders in Israelite society who performed ceremonies and sacrifices in the temple.
The seventh day of the week, on which God rested after creating the world, and which the Israelites were to keep holy.
